newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend surge, seen down on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend surge, seen down on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares set their third consecutive 34-month high on Monday but analysts said the strong selling after price-fixing signalled the bourse should begin a brief profit-taking correction on Tuesday.
"It seems at most we should have a two-day break...taking the market down a few hundred points," said Emil Onyszczuk, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
The bourse rose 0.8 percent on Monday after surging 8.4 percent last week and 31 percent since mid-January, with foreign investors apparently acting on their fresh picks for 1997, analysts said.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.8 percent to 17,603.9 points and turnover rose 13.2 percent to 290.1 million zlotys ($96.6 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 61 to 13 with 14 stocks flat.

Analysts said good signs were Friday's news that Poland's industrial climate in the manufacturing sector improved in January and Monday's news that food prices rose 1.5 percent that month, when price rises are sometimes higher.

They said top gainer Optimus extended Friday's surge by nearly the daily maximum 10 percent after the computer firm said on Thursday it had received orders to convert 159 of its convertible bonds, freeing reserves and upping January profit.
Analysts said builder Mostostal Krakow, up 9.7 percent, was benefiting from demand amid low liquidity, as the firm, which did not conduct an IPO, was in relatively few hands.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose 3.7 percent to 170 zlotys ($56.6) in regular trade and were flat at 165 zlotys ($55) in 30.8-million-zloty ($10.3 million) continuous trade, where stock turnover was at 15.2 million zlotys ($5.1 million).
